chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no muʾmin except that Allah has assigned to him four satans who tempt him, intending to lead him astray; and a disbeliever who seeks to attack him; and a muʾmin who envies him—and he is the hardest of them upon him; and a hypocrite who follows his slips.

key_terms.شَيَاطِينَ: devilish forces that tempt and mislead
key_terms.مُنَافِقًا: a hypocrite who outwardly shows faith while concealing opposition
key_terms.يَحْسُدُهُ: envies him for what he has

ai.seo_question: What kinds of enemies and trials surround a muʾmin according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a muʾmin is surrounded by multiple forms of trial and opposition, including satanic temptation, hostility from a disbeliever, envy from another believer, and scrutiny from a hypocrite. It highlights the difficulty of the believer’s path and the need for patience, vigilance, and steadfastness.
